supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded a Kerberos service-ticket request for svc-bkp from 45.79.19.196, an external IP address; shortly afterward, FILE-HD-01 recorded a successful svc-bkp service logon. The inventory says there is no VPN and remote administration is restricted to WS-OHADDAD-01, making this authentication pattern inconsistent with the stated environment.

FILE-HD-01 subsequently launched the approved CobaltVault agent as svc-bkp with the Nightly job and an ingest.cobaltvault.net target. This is consistent with an authorized backup workflow, but it does not explain why the preceding svc-bkp ticket request came from an external IP.

The available proxy records for the CobaltVault connection show reported tunnel byte counts of 1,099 client-to-server and 48,593 server-to-client bytes; they do not document a transfer of hundreds of MB.

At 13:46, FILE-HD-01 made an SMB connection to DC-HD-01 that coincided with an ANONYMOUS LOGON network logon. The recorded connection was small, and these records alone do not show what SMB resource or data was accessed.

That the CobaltVault agent was misused; its recorded execution and destination are consistent with the approved backup workflow.
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate DC authentication records and network telemetry for 45.79.19.196, including the source connection, authentication details, and any related svc-bkp activity.
Obtain firewall, proxy, and network-flow records with complete byte counts and destinations for FILE-HD-01 around 13:20–14:20 UTC.
Review CobaltVault job and audit logs to verify whether a backup ran, what data it handled, and whether the observed session was expected.
Review FILE-HD-01 service-account logon history, svc-bkp credential changes, and relevant service or scheduled-task configuration.
